key_insight: Higher-resolution Meteosat Third Generation (MTG/FCI) imagery improves CNN-based surface solar irradiance retrieval mainly when clouds are the dominant driver of variability.
engineering_relevance: For photovoltaic monitoring and forecasting, the hybrid SEVIRI-FCI model can deliver more accurate 10-minute irradiance estimates than MSG/SEVIRI alone in cloudy conditions, improving operational solar resource inputs.
method: Multi-imager CNN combining MSG/SEVIRI and MTG/FCI satellite imagery
Uses solar-geometry and clear-sky irradiance features
Evaluated with site-based cross-validation and multiple training seeds against pyranometer data
evidence_signal: Validated against ground pyranometer measurements from eight Estonian stations and compared with SARAH-3; the hybrid model reduced RMSE by 8.2 W m^-2 in overcast and 5.7 W m^-2 in cloudy conditions.
watch_item: Higher spatial resolution alone did not fix clear-sky or partly cloudy limitations, so gains may be conditional and not uniform across sky conditions.
paper_title: Meteosat Third Generation imagery improves CNN-based SSI retrieval
